# Ebola outbreak becomes deadliest in DR Congo’s history

Health

The Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is now the deadliest the country has ever faced, the UN’s World Health Organization (WHO) said on Monday. [...] Tweet URL

A total of 730 patients remain in isolation or in the hospital and 1,040 people have recovered from the disease, and the fatality rate has risen to 46 per cent, according to Government data.

The current outbreak remains eclipsed only by West Africa’s 2014-2016 Ebola outbreak, which saw 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths, according to WHO, but the Bundibugyo outbreak is taking lives at a much faster rate. [...] Vaccine trials are underway in the UK and Canada as the Bundibugyo strain has no approved treatment.

Inadequate health infrastructure, ongoing conflict at the epicentre of the outbreak and distrust of medical authorities have all hindered efforts to help as WHO warns the outbreak is “outpacing the response.”

# Ebola update in the DRC

Robert Herriman

The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reports through May 27, 125 cumulative confirmed cases of Bundibugyo Ebolavirus have been detected in three provinces- 110 in Ituri, 14 in North Kivu, and 1 in South Kivu. [...] The following health zones were affected: In Ituri, 7 out of 36 Health Zones affected (Aru, Bunia, Kilo, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Nizi, and Nyankunde). In North Kivu, 5 out of 35 Health Zones affected (Goma, Butembo, Oicha, Kalunguta, and Katwa) and in South Kiva, 1 out of 34 Health Zones were affected (Miti-Murhesa)

A total of 906 suspected cases were also reported.
